texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Sh. Ibrahim suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 13.01.2020 at about 18.30 pm, petitioner/injured Ibrahim was riding a motorcycle bearing no.DL-9SDW-2634 and one Salman as pillion rider. When they reached towards Nangal Mau, near Nangla Cheeta, PS Kasganj, a speeding tempo/three wheeler /Bajaj Auto without any registration number (having engine no.BHYWKF12399) came at a high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle on which the victim was riding. Due to the impact, victim Ibrahim got serious injuries. He was removed to District Hospital, Kajganj from where he was referred to Aligarh Hospital and Safdarjang Hospital, Delhi for treatment. 3. An FIR no.0033/20 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC, PS Kasganj, Distt-Kasganj, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 2 Of 26 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:50:37 Date: 2025.02.08 +0530 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Written statement was filed by respondent no. 1 and 2 denying rash and negligence on the part of respondent no.1. It has been pleaded that respondent no.1 is son of respondent no.2 and that at the time of the accident the offending vehicle was allotted a temporary number i.e. UP-87T-4714. It has been pleaded that respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle with due care and caution and in supervision of one Devinder who was having a valid driving licence. It has further been pleaded that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of the motorcycle who suddenly emerged from the wrong side and dashed into the offending vehicle. It has been pleaded by the respondents that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the insurance company and that respondent no.1 was having a valid learners' driving licence. In its reply respondent no.3/insurance company has denied its liability to indemnify the insured /respondent no.2 or compensate the petitioner in case respondents were found to be in breach of the insurance policy. Respondent no.3 has denied that the respondent no.1 was holding a valid driving licence and that even the learners licence held by him was not applicable to the class /category of vehicle being driven by him at the time of accident. 6. Vide order dated 20.12.2022, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 3 Of 26 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA road traffic accident on 13.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle Bajaj Auto Three Wheeler Tempo Engine no. Ibrahim vs Jeetu on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180425577/ 2 BHYWKF123899 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Ibrahim led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testifies on the lines of the claim petition. He further deposed that on 13.01.2020 at about 06:30 p.m., PW-1 was riding a motorcycle bearing no. DL-9SWD-2634, one Salman was pillion rider. He deposed that while going towards Nangal Mau, Nangloi after crossing Kasganj town a speeding tempo/three wheeler/Bajaj Auto engine no. BHYWKF12399 (without any registration number mentioned) came from opposite directions, in gross violation to speed without giving any horn or signal, trespassed into the lane of motorcycle against the flow of traffic and hit the motorcycle no.DL-9SDW-2634, resulting in the road accident. He further deposed that due to the impact he received grievous injuries. He stated that he was take to District Hospital Kasganj thereafter he removed to the Aligarh Hospital where his MLC was prepared and later he was referred to Safdarjung Hospital. He further deposed that he has incurred expenses on medical treatment /test and pharmacy to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- but all the bills could not be preserved and protected and are not traceable due to trauma, bills in possession are of Rs.20,529/- MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 4 Of 26 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.08 Date: 04:50:47 +0530 only as Ex.PW1/4. He deposed that he was also examined by Disability Board and assessed 47% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb and right lower limb as Ex.PW1/5. He deposed that he was working as a driver at Delhi and earning of Rs.35,000/- per month. The driving licence as Ex.PW1/6 and Badge issued by Transport Department as Ex.PW1/7. He relied upon his Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/1 (OSR), certified copy of criminal case as Ex.PW1/2, discharge summary as Ex.PW1/3, Bill summary along with original bills of Rs.20529/- as Ex.PW1/4 (colly), disability certificate as Ex.PW1/5, copy of driving licence as Ex.PW1/6, copy of Badge issued by Transport Authority as Ex.PW1/7, copy of PAN card as Ex.PW1/8 (OSR) and copy of registration certificate of car bearing no.DL1ZC-0377 as ex.PW1/9 (OSR). He was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. Respondent no.3 /insurance company led his evidence by examining one Mukul Thakur as R3W1. R3W1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R3W1/A. He deposed that the a u t o T S R h a v i n g E n g i n e n o . OG-20-4691-1803-00000322 dated 19.09.2019 issued for the period from 19.09.2019 to 18.09.2020 midnight is in the name of respondent. He relied upon copy of the insurance policy dated 19.09.2019 as Ex.R3W1/1. He deposed that respondent no.1 /driver was not holding a valid driving licence a the time of accident which is in contravention to Section 3 of the M V Act and the same is also a clear breach of MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 5 Of 26 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.08 04:50:52 +0530 the terms and conditions of the insurance policy. He further deposed that respondent no.3 /insurance company issued notice u/O 12 Rule 8 of CPC to driver Mr. Jeetu to produce the original valid driving licence, however no driving licence has been produced by him. He also relied upon the notice and postal receipt as Ex.R3W1/2 and Ex.R3W1/3 respectively. R3W1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for petitioner. No evidence was led on behalf of the respondent no.1 and 2. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: . Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. On the other hand, it has been argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that the petitioner has relied upon a copy of a learners driving licence that respondent no.1 was holding at the time of the accident. In Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited And Others (2018) 7 SCC 558 is relevant to the present facts and quoted as under: ''...15. We may fruitfully note that the three-Judge Bench adverted to situations where the driver does not have a licence and the same has been allowed to be driven by the MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 10 Of 26 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.02.08 04:51:12 +0530 owner of the vehicle by such person, the insurer would be entitled to succeed in defence and avoid liability, but the position would be different where the disputed question of fact arises as to whether the driver had a valid licence and where the owner of the vehicle committed a breach of the terms of the contract of insurance as also the provisions of the Act by consciously allowing any person to drive a vehicle who did not have a valid driving licence." It was further observed: ''...24. Nothing has been brought on record by the insured to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle. In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer. Therefore, the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed that the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver. The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle...''.. 15. In such circumstances, the liability of compensation falls primarily upon the driver and owner of the offending vehicle bearing engine no.BHYWKF123899. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is MACT NO.219/20 Ibrahim v. Jitu & Ors. P.No. 11 Of 26 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.02.08 04:51:16 +0530 that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: "10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
